depth_first_rationale: The customer raises the card replacement only after the agent confirms the dispute details, and asks about the refund timeline only after the card cancellation is confirmed — never bundling concerns.
uncertainty_rationale: The customer appropriately hedges on the amount ('like $89.21 i think') despite the scenario being certain fraud, which is realistic since people may not remember exact figures, while remaining assertive about non-recognition ('yes 100% wasnt me').
info_drip_rationale: The customer reveals date, amount, and merchant only when directly prompted by the agent, and even withholds the merchant name authentically by saying they don't recognize it before the agent pulls up transactions.
pragmatic_rationale: Turns like 'thats the thing i dont recognize it at all. something weird i've never heard of' and 'when do i get my money back' read as natural, colloquial caller speech rather than scripted phrasing.
persona_score_rationale: The terse, calm, intermediate-knowledge persona is consistently present — short responses, no panic, no jargon, and no over-explanation — exemplified by single-line confirmations like 'the freedom one' and 'yes thats it. never heard of them'.
